assumptions: 12 warehouses in 6 regions; 2500 products in 5 categories; 250 suppliers in 7 countries.
Each supplier serves exactly 1 category; every FG PO line is placed with the product's primary supplier (share 1.0).

FG receipt delay is uniform-like over -3..14 days and does NOT follow reliability (spearman -0.0108). Existing FG rows are left as-is; causality (reliability, lead time, country shocks) is imposed on the NEW RM side, and FG-side events are mined as statistical clusters.
'Late' for anchoring = delay >= 7 days (median positive delay).
Demand is intermittent: 13.1% of product-weeks and 1.16% of product-warehouse-weeks have sales; product_demand_weekly is therefore stored sparsely (weeks with demand or a non-zero forecast).
Pareto skew in source sales is weak (top 20% SKUs = 27.2% of units); fulfilled demand must equal existing sales exactly, so the skew is inherited, not imposed.
Stock hits <= 0 on only 25 product-warehouse-days (14 pairs); most unfulfilled demand must therefore be explained by logged shock events (allocations, DC disruptions, demand spikes).
Expected make products ~1125 (category make-probabilities in config); spares-like categories are buy-only.
For make products the FG PO is treated as the replenishment order from the assigned plant; the PO's supplier is the tolling partner operating the line.
No SQLite was provided when the input is a CSV folder; the output SQLite is built from the unchanged CSV contents plus the new tables.
